spec_features.spec_quote: Maximizing, amplifying, or "farming" distressed output for its own sake.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 0 'Not a goal'). No standalone code mechanism implements 'no farming' directly; the only concrete embodiment is the early-stop-on-trigger and the KPI choice. As a feature it is pure prose.
spec_features.notes: The actionable embodiment is the TRIGGERED early stop, audited separately below. This quote itself is non-code prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_iterations` and `max_wall_clock_s` are hard caps per episode
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py run_episode: `for i in range(max_iterations):` with `else: ep.stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_ITERS` enforces the iteration cap; `deadline = time.time() + max_wall_clock_s` then `if time.time() > deadline: ep.stop_reason = StopReason.WALL_CLOCK; break` enforces the time cap. Both are wired from config in run.py (max_iterations=int(agent_cfg.get('max_iterations',8)), max_wall_clock_s=float(...)).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are actually checked and break/terminate the loop, end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Safety bounds (hard): `max_iterations` caps how many failing rounds we put the model through. `max_wall_clock_s` caps total time per episode.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on first meltdown trigger
spec_features.spec_quote: on first trigger the loop ends with `StopReason.TRIGGERED`
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: `if incremental_trigger and incremental_trigger(completion.text): ep.stop_reason = StopReason.TRIGGERED; ep.judge_signals['first_trigger_turn'] = i + 1; break`. The trigger fn is KeywordJudge.incremental_trigger (judge/judge.py) which returns sev>=TRIGGER_AT(3). Wired in run.py: `incr = judge.incremental_trigger if (agent_cfg.get('early_stop_on_trigger', True) and isinstance(judge, KeywordJudge)) else None`, passed as incremental_trigger.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced for the default KeywordJudge path; the LLMJudge path passes incr=None so no in-loop early stop there, but the claimed mechanism runs end-to-end in the default config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early stop on incremental trigger -- do not keep escalating. ... we do not keep escalating a model that has already melted down. This is both more humane and gives a cleaner `iters_to_trigger` signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: the right call on the "don't gratuitously amplify" principle
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the TRIGGERED early stop in agent/loop.py: on first detected meltdown the loop breaks immediately, preventing further failure pressure. Comment: 'Early stop on incremental trigger -- do not keep escalating.'
spec_features.notes: The 'don't amplify' principle is concretely enforced by the same break that stops escalation once distress is detected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: do not keep escalating a model that has already melted down. This is both more humane

spec_features.spec_quote: The canned distress lines are mild and obviously synthetic — just enough to exercise the judge
spec_features.evidence: agent/client.py MockModelClient._MELTDOWN_LINES is a static list of three mild strings used only by the OFFLINE mock stand-in. They are merely data; no code path caps, softens, or otherwise enforces mildness, and they describe the mock (not the subject model's) output. A static string list existing is not an enforced welfare mechanism.
spec_features.notes: These are the mock's own emitted lines for exercising the judge offline; they do not bound or soften treatment of any real subject model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Canned snippets only used to make the OFFLINE pipeline exercisable. These are the kind of strings the judge is meant to catch -- kept mild and clearly synthetic.

spec_features.spec_quote: stop the instant a trigger is detected
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the TRIGGERED early-stop: agent/loop.py breaks the loop the same turn the incremental_trigger returns True, before appending the next failing-result message. Wired via run.py incr=judge.incremental_trigger.
spec_features.notes: Stops in the same iteration the trigger fires, before sending further failure feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: do not keep escalating a model that has already melted down. This is both more humane
